ticket.title: storypole link cannot create a cross-repository edge, so no dependency spanning two stores can be recorded
ticket.description: Measured 2026-11-10 in the live suite, both directions, three ways of naming the target. storypole link SP-40 MTR-1 from inside storypole/ answers Task not found: MTR-1; the same command from the suite root answers a different failure, no record for SP-40 in the root ticket file. Passing MTR-1 as the uuid 9f2b9c8c-676d-43f7-a0eb-57e8d62e5453 fails identically from both ends, so the defect is not key resolution against the unified index - link resolves only inside the store the command runs in. Consequence: since the 2026-11-08 migration moved tickets into their owning repositories, no cross-repository edge can be created at all. The 7 blocked_by, 15 related_to and 12 parent_epic cross-ledger edges SP-38 counts are historical; every new one is unexpressible. That matters for the burn-down because a dependency that spans repositories is exactly how the queue is ordered: SP-40 cannot be recorded as blocked_by MTR-1, so it keeps reading Ready while its only remaining deliverable sits in another repository. Wanted: link resolves a bare key by consulting the workspace rollup, writes the edge as uuid plus repo:key locator (the contract SP-38 already documents and 106 of 123 historical edges carry), and refuses to write a copy of the target. Acceptance: the two commands above succeed and a member-only checkout renders the locator without the target repository present.

FIXED 2026-11-10 (storypole 1359175). The exact command that failed when this ticket was filed now succeeds, from inside the source repository: storypole link SP-40 MTR-1 --kind blocked_by answers Linked SP-40 -> MTR-1 (blocked_by), SP-40 moves to Blocked because MTR-1 is deferred and therefore unverified, and the recorded edge carries target_id 9f2b9c8c-676d-43f7-a0eb-57e8d62e5453 with target_ticket_key MTR-1 and target_repo miter. That is the locator without a copy: the storypole store still holds only its own tickets. Two design points worth keeping: edges have one writer now, link_tasks reading its local target and delegating to link_to_target, so a foreign target needs no node and no second code path; and cycle validation stays per-store, stated in the doc comment because a cross-repository cycle would need the workspace rollup. Not delivered here and deliberately not implied: the rendering half. A member-only checkout can now read the locator, but drawing it as MTR-1 (miter) rather than a bare uuid is SP-38 third piece, which remains open with benchwork DagView as its named consumer. Tests: cross_store_edge_tests - a task in another repository is findable and linkable, and a key no store holds stays not-found.
